[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone—thanks for hopping on. quick rollcall?
[00:08] Jared Molina: Hey yeah this is Jared — CTO at Klaxon. Priya and Sasha are here too.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi all.
[00:14] Sasha Li: Sasha, ML eng.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Great. Maya from Redwood AE, with Eric SE and Lena on support. We planned an autopsy of the sprint runs and to talk routing.
[00:29] Eric Patel: I'll start with results real quick — caveat that some of the labels in the dashboard got munged, sorry. We ran three steady-state passes and two spike passes against your test harness.
[00:37] [00:37] Eric Patel: Pass 1 (steady) p50 was 38 ms lower than BaselineAI, p95 about 12% better. Pass 2 had a p95 regression to roughly parity — we think that's due to KV cache warmup and small burst behavior.
[00:54] [00:54] Sasha Li: Are those numbers with quantized weights? We used INT8 in the lab runs.
[00:58] Eric Patel: Yes INT8 on Redwood’s optimized kernel path; same quant config as the worksheet you shared but we used slightly larger batch windows during low-load to push throughput.
[01:12] [01:12] Priya Rao: During the spike runs BaselineAI held steady at p95 220 ms while Redwood jumped to 320 for two minutes — that was our main concern.
[01:23] Eric Patel: Right — that's the regression point. Two root causes we see: first, routing kept sending full-length requests to the same slot causing KV eviction during those bursts; second, autoscale cooldown settings were conservative so we saw queueing until new workers came up.
[01:37] [01:37] Jared Molina: So is this fixable with config changes or do we need dedicated capacity?
[01:42] Maya Chen: Good question. There are three levers: routing / fallback thresholds, cache/prefix pinning, and using a small dedicated slot for burst hedging. For most clients, routing + prefix pin is enough.
[01:53] [01:53] Omar Khan: What's the operational burden of prefix pinning? Won't that increase memory and cost?
[01:58] Eric Patel: Slight bump in memory yes — but pin only high-value prefixes (top N frequent queries). We can provide a script to surface candidate prefixes. For Klaxon we estimate <8% memory increase vs 15–20% latency improvement at p95 during bursts.
[02:14] [02:14] Priya Rao: On cost, BaselineAI charges per-VM per-hour; Redwood's unit economics look better but we need that delta at our 500qps scaling curve.
[02:25] Maya Chen: We'll send a delta sheet for your exact traffic shape. Key point: if you offload burst to a tiny dedicated slot, avg unit cost still below BaselineAI at your runrate, but we'll show numbers.
[02:38] [02:38] Sasha Li: Can you explain the fallback playbook? We had a failover test and BaselineAI degraded gracefully, returning a simplified response.
[02:46] Eric Patel: Redwood supports a fallback policy: route to a cheaper model variant or to cached completions when latency exceeds threshold. For Klaxon we recommend: primary → lightweight quant variant (lower context) → cached answer → simplify output (shorter tokens). That gives graceful degradation without 500ms spikes.
[03:05] [03:05] Jared Molina: Any vendor lock or compatibility concerns with our existing prompt templates?
[03:10] Maya Chen: No lock. The only change is slight prompt truncation for low-latency fallbacks; we can parameterize that so your app toggles the mode.
[03:18] [03:18] Priya Rao: Security — KMS and SAML. Are those in our Private plan or can they be done on Hosted?
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: Good question — we support KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated. Hosted can work with envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KMS; for strict audit requirements you'd pick Dedicated or Private.
[03:36] [03:36] Omar Khan: We need full audit logs and SAML SSO. Also data residency for EU workloads.
[03:41] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll include the SOC2/ISO docs and a mapping for logs retention. Also propose a security deep-dive next week.
[03:51] [03:51] Sasha Li: Back to the numbers: can you share the exact p95 histogram? The dashboard clipped some buckets.
[03:57] Eric Patel: We'll export full histograms and the raw traces. Expect CSVs with percentiles and a column for model variant, batch size, and KV hit ratio.
[04:09] [04:09] Priya Rao: One oddity — on run 3 we saw a steady drop in throughput at 30 minutes, not spikes. Memory leak?
[04:16] Eric Patel: We dug into that: it looks like ephemeral memory pressure on the slot because of a non-uniform sequence length distribution in your testset. When long-tail sequences arrive, they hog KV and reduce throughput. Two mitigations: sequence bucketing (separate workers for long sequences) or request-level length limits.
[04:33] [04:33] Jared Molina: Sequence bucketing sounds operationally heavier. What's the cost tradeoff?
[04:38] Eric Patel: Slight complexity — adds one routing rule. Cost-wise, keeping long sequences isolated prevents them from inflating p95 for short queries; overall unit cost for short queries improves which matters for most of your traffic.
[04:51] [04:51] Priya Rao: For the VPC peering test, we had trouble getting baseline egress metrics. Any tips?
[04:57] Maya Chen: We'll provide a minimal test harness that produces comparable metrics and a checklist for VPC flow logs. Also, Jared — you offered a peering window?
[05:04] Jared Molina: Yes, we're aiming for Friday night maintenance window to peer and run two shaded-load tests.
[05:09] [05:09] Maya Chen: Great — schedule that and we'll stand by.
[05:12] Eric Patel: Quick note on batch tuning: your current client batches at 16, but Redwood's adaptive batching suggests 8–12 for best p95 under variable traffic. That change alone reduced p95 by ~18% in our lab.
[05:26] Sasha Li: Hmm our client software is opinionated; we'd need a small client patch. Can you supply a patch or an SDK config flag?
[05:33] Eric Patel: Yes — small client-side knob; also a server-side throttle if you can't change the client. We'll push a sample.
[05:39] [05:39] Lena Ortiz: I'll add that as an action item — share the SDK config and runnable example.
[05:45] [06:00] -- 10-minute technical deep dive segment clipped in transcription --
[15:12] Eric Patel: Returning to routing decision — recommendation: two-hour dedicated hedging slot during peak hours for 2 weeks to prove stability. If p95 improves to target, we can rollback routing. This is cheaper than full reserved capacity.
[15:28] Jared Molina: Two-hour slot, is that per-day or per-peak?
[15:31] Eric Patel: Per-peak window; we can automate scale up/down. It's effectively a burst buffer.
[15:36] [15:36] Priya Rao: We'll need clear SLO targets before approving any paid slot. Our SLO is p95 < 250 ms for interactive calls.
[15:44] Maya Chen: Agreed — Redwood proposes p95 target 220 ms for tier-1 requests during the hedging window. We'll publish the acceptance criteria.
[15:54] [15:54] Omar Khan: Could the baseline vendor match that with a cheaper config?
[15:58] Maya Chen: Possibly — BaselineAI has different overheads; our differentiation is predictable unit economics and tooling to keep p95 under control. We'll show the cost curve.
[16:10] [16:10] Sasha Li: For the security deep dive, can we scope which logs you retain on-hosted vs dedicated? We need log-level retention mapping.
[16:17] Lena Ortiz: We'll attach a retention mapping and sample logs. Hosted has shorter retention by default; Dedicated/Private meets typical enterprise retention windows.
[16:26] [16:26] Jared Molina: Any red flags with our test harness? We saw a small mismatch in header encoding for some requests.
[16:33] Eric Patel: We noted that; some multipart boundaries looked different and caused longer pre-processing times in our load generator. That explains a small tail. Fixing that should shave another 10–15 ms.
[16:45] [16:45] Priya Rao: Ok — so next steps: we want CSVs, config artifacts, client patch, and two controlled runs during peering window. Also a security deep dive.
[16:56] Maya Chen: Yes exactly. We'll also include a short runbook for prefix pinning and sequence bucketing suggestions.
[17:03] [17:03] Jared Molina: Timeline-wise—assuming we get artifacts by Friday, run on Saturday, security deep dive the week after — does that work?
[17:09] Maya Chen: Works for us.
[17:12] [17:12] Sasha Li: One last question—any known compatibility issues with our telemetry stack (OpenTelemetry collectors)?
[17:18] Eric Patel: We integrate with OTLP; just ensure collector spans are forwarded and we can correlate trace IDs. We'll include an example config.
[17:27] [17:27] Priya Rao: Perfect.
[17:30] Maya Chen: Alright let's recap: Redwood to share histograms, raw traces, config, client patch, cost delta sheet; Klaxon to run two shaded tests during peering window and confirm SAML/KMS constraints for security call.
[17:47] Jared Molina: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[17:50] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in cadence and post notes to the workspace.
[18:00] -- call ends --
